title: Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.
shortTitle: Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.
summary: The reward advertisement invited performance without advance notification of acceptance.
notes: The company promised £100 after specified use if illness followed and pointed to a £1,000 bank deposit as evidence of seriousness. Carlill used the product, became ill, and recovered. The court inferred from the transaction that notice in advance was dispensed with. The notes distinguish the requested use from illness as a condition of the obligation to pay.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 228–229. Open assigned page 228.
